title: Final Project Blueprint 📋
description: Plan, structure, and debug a complete page before you code.

slides.title: From Idea to Code 🧠
slides.content:
# The Planning Phase

Jumping into code without a plan leads to frustration. Follow this process:
1. **Sketch the layout** on paper or a whiteboard – identify the main sections.
2. **Choose semantic HTML** for each section (header, nav, main, aside, footer).
3. **Define the CSS Grid/Flexbox structure** – decide which parent containers are grid or flex.
4. **List components** (card, button, form) and plan their classes (e.g., BEM naming).
5. **Identify breakpoints** – where does the design need to change?
6. **Build mobile‑first**, adding complexity with media queries.

slides.title: Structuring Your CSS 📁
slides.content:
# Organise Your Styles

- **Reset/Normalize** – box‑sizing, margin/padding.
- **Base** – typography, body styles, headings.
- **Layout** – grid/flex containers, main sections.
- **Components** – buttons, cards, forms, navigation.
- **Utilities** – helper classes (e.g., `.text-center`, `.hidden`).
- **Media Queries** – grouped with the components they modify, or at the end.

Use CSS comments (`/* section */`) to separate areas.

slides.title: Example CSS Structure
Debugging Common Issues 🐛
slides.content:
# When Things Go Wrong

- **Layout broken?** Check for missing `border-box` reset, margin collapse, or wrong `position`.
- **Element not visible?** Maybe `display: none`, `opacity: 0`, `visibility: hidden`, or `z-index` issue.
- **Spacing uneven?** Look at margin vs padding, `gap` not set, or extra margins from defaults.
- **Grid/Flex not working?** Verify `display` is set on parent; only direct children are affected.
- **Image not loading?** Check `src` path, file extension, and case sensitivity.

Use browser DevTools – the computed styles panel and layout highlights are your best friends.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Version Control

Save versions of your project (even as separate files). When you try a new approach, you can always go back. Even better, learn Git – it's essential for real projects.
